The pacing of the story feels very natural, deliberate, and well-balanced. The narrative primarily unfolds in a tight, immediate scene—covering only a few minutes in "story time" at the ferry dock—which is slightly stretched through rich sensory details (the smell of oil and wet wood, the brown water carrying a shoe, the crunching of the metal crank) and quiet observations. This slowing down of the present moment effectively highlights the unspoken tension and emotional distance between Ilse and Jonas. 

At the same time, the author uses brief, seamless moments of time compression to provide decades of backstory without interrupting the flow of the present scene. Thirty years of the engine's history and the years that have passed since Jonas left at age seventeen (implied by his now "soft hands" and suit jacket) are condensed into a few Passing thoughts. This interplay between the stretched, quiet present and the compressed history gives the short story remarkable depth and emotional weight.
